ImageSpeech needs the camera to work.
Gemma could not start on this phone. Using local OCR.

Download Google\'s Gemma 4 E2B model once to read and answer typed or spoken questions entirely on this phone. Photos never leave the device. Spoken questions are turned into text by the phone\'s speech recognizer, which runs on the phone when one is available. The model needs about 2.6 GB of storage and a few gigabytes of free memory while running. Without it, local OCR reads text.
Gemma is off: this phone ran out of memory while using it. Using local OCR.
This phone has limited memory, so Gemma runs on the CPU and loads after each photo is taken. The first answer can take about 40 seconds; follow-ups are faster.
Delete the downloaded Gemma model? Questions will be unavailable until you download it again. Local reading keeps working.
Questions need the on-device Gemma model. See Processing settings. Tap Take photo to read with local OCR.
Microphone access is ready. Hold the button again and speak.
Microphone access was denied. You can still type a question.
Processing mode changed. Start the request again.
Microphone muted. You can still type questions.
The microphone is muted. Unmute it with the microphone button on the camera screen, or type your question.
To ask questions out loud, allow ImageSpeech to use the microphone in the app\'s settings.
Edit your profile and dietary restrictions.

Type any dietary restrictions or allergies. After you take a photo of food, ImageSpeech tells you if it looks like it contains any of them. Your profile is stored only on this phone and never leaves it.
For example: allergic to walnuts. I don\'t eat meat.
Checking photos needs the on-device Gemma model. Download it in Processing settings.
Checks can miss things, especially when the ingredients are not in the photo. For a serious allergy, always read the label yourself.
Stopped. Ask a question, Summarize, or Read all text.
Say the text in the box at the top again.
